abstract: A survey of 787 creative professionals conducted by the Society of Authors (UK) in January 2024 found that generative AI has already caused significant work loss for illustrators and translators, with 26% of illustrators and 36% of translators reporting lost work. Large majorities expect future income decline, with 78% of illustrators and 77% of translators anticipating further negative impacts on their earnings from creative work.
keyFindings: 26% of illustrators and 36% of translators have already lost work due to generative AI.
78% of illustrators and 77% of translators expect generative AI will negatively impact their future income.
65% of fiction writers and 57% of non-fiction writers believe generative AI will negatively impact future income from their creative work.
86% of respondents are concerned about their style, voice and likeness being mimicked or reproduced in generative AI output.
Only 8% of translators and 5% of illustrators have used generative AI in their work because their publisher or commissioning organisation asked them to.
methodology: Survey of 787 respondents conducted throughout January 2024 by The Society of Authors (UK) among its 12,500 members and other authors. Respondents included writers of fiction and non-fiction, scriptwriters, poets, journalists, illustrators, and translators at various career stages and publishing arrangements (traditionally and self-published).
